abstract.label: Background
abstract.text: Creatine is a compound that the body makes and stores, mostly in muscle, as a reserve of quick energy. Researchers have studied it for more than 30 years, mainly in people who train. It is now also being tested for memory, mood and brain disease. In 2026, a trial reported that people gained lean mass on creatine without exercise, and that result came from 13 people on creatine.

abstract.label: Purpose
abstract.text: This article checks what the published research shows about creatine in people who do not exercise. It also shows how strong that evidence is.

abstract.label: What the evidence shows
abstract.text: Shown. Creatine treats two rare inherited conditions in which the body cannot make it. Promising but small. One small trial found better test scores after a night without sleep, at one very large dose. Small trials also found a benefit in depression when creatine was added to treatment, but confidence in that result is very low. Tested, no clear benefit. The larger trials found no clear gain in muscle or memory in people who do not exercise. Two large trials also found that creatine did not slow Parkinson's or Huntington's disease.

abstract.label: What this means for you
abstract.text: If you do not exercise, the evidence gives no reason to expect a noticeable change in your body or your thinking from creatine. Its clear benefit comes with weight training.
